question: One week after delivery, a 3550-g (7-lb 13-oz) newborn has multiple episodes of bilious vomiting and abdominal distention. He passed urine 14 hours after delivery and had his first bowel movement 3 days after delivery. He was born at term to a 31-year-old woman. Pregnancy was uncomplicated and the mother received adequate prenatal care. His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 132/min, and respirations are 50/min. Examination shows a distended abdomen. Bowel sounds are hypoactive. Digital rectal examination shows a patent anus and an empty rectum. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. An x-ray of the abdomen is shown. Which of the following is the underlying cause of these findings?

options.opa: Defective migration of neural crest cells
options.opb: Disruption of blood flow to the fetal jejunum
options.ope: Failed recanalization of the fetal duodenum

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Newborn presents with bilious vomiting" -> "Indicates possible intestinal obstruction" -> "Abdominal distention observed" -> "Empty rectum on examination" -> "Suggests obstruction proximal to rectum" -> "Failed recanalization of the fetal duodenum is a known cause" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Newborn has multiple episodes of bilious vomiting" -> "Bilious vomiting suggests bile is present in the stomach" -> "Presence of bile indicates obstruction in the intestinal tract" -> "Distended abdomen and hypoactive bowel sounds" -> "Empty rectum suggests obstruction" -> "Failed recanalization of the fetal duodenum leads to obstruction" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Newborn exhibits abdominal distention" -> "Distention indicates accumulation of gas or fluid" -> "Hypoactive bowel sounds suggest decreased intestinal activity" -> "Empty rectum on examination" -> "Indicates obstruction in the bowel" -> "Failed recanalization of the fetal duodenum is a common cause of such obstruction" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Newborn has delayed passage of meconium" -> "Delayed meconium passage can indicate obstruction" -> "Bilious vomiting and abdominal distention present" -> "Empty rectum on examination" -> "Failed recanalization of the fetal duodenum is a likely cause" -> 75%
analysis: The clinical presentation of the newborn, including bilious vomiting, abdominal distention, and the finding of an empty rectum on digital examination, suggests a significant gastrointestinal obstruction. The timing of the first bowel movement (3 days after delivery) is also indicative of a potential obstruction. The most likely underlying cause of these findings is 'failed recanalization of the fetal duodenum,' which is associated with duodenal atresia. This condition is characterized by the failure of the duodenum to recanalize during fetal development, leading to obstruction. The other options, while they may cause gastrointestinal issues, do not align as closely with the specific symptoms and findings presented in this case.
normal_results: Hirschsprung Disease CAUSES Neonatal intestinal obstruction
